properties.project_name: Arthur and Toni Rembe Rock Hall
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-18 for Mission Bay's UCSF campus pass: real OSM building footprint. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the notes were corrected in place: the Japanese seismic technology was buckling-restrained braces (Forell: 'we worked directly with Nippon Steel in Japan to design and procure Buckling-Restrained Braces ... brand new to California seismic engineering practice'), not base isolation; '171,600 sq ft' appears in no source read (Forell gives 165,000; the May 2000 Regents item gives 170,965 gsf). The April 2005 design-award mention rests on a UCSF news page that returns 403 to automated fetches (only its URL slug was seen). 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint, not a hand trace or plan estimate. This is the opposite situation from Mission Bay's condo-mapped residential towers (Avalon, Radiance, etc.): here, ONE large Assessor land parcel spans SEVERAL UCSF buildings (confirmed against data/raw/parcels.geojson and DataSF's Assessor tax roll -- e.g. blklot 8711507 at 675 Nelson Rising Lane alone is ~13 acres, far larger than any single building on it), so using the parcel boundary per building would make multiple records overlap and double-count the same ground. The real building footprint is the only non-overlapping, honest shape for each one.'. 2026-10-12: accuracy audit (round 4c) fix. notes: 'Opening year is genuinely contested across sources (2002 vs. 2004 vs. one secondary '2005' reference); 2004 is the best-supported reading ...' now reads 'Opened 2004 per UCSF's history timeline', because no cited source gives 2002 or 2005 (the 2026-10-06 changelog row had already corrected the milestone; this notes text was not updated then). The April 2005 design-award mention is no longer used as support, since the UCSF page behind it could not be read. No change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type.
properties.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint, not a hand trace or plan estimate. This is the opposite situation from Mission Bay's condo-mapped residential towers (Avalon, Radiance, etc.): here, ONE large Assessor land parcel spans SEVERAL UCSF buildings (confirmed against DataSF's Assessor parcel data and tax roll -- e.g. blklot 8711507 at 675 Nelson Rising Lane alone is ~13 acres, far larger than any single building on it), so using the parcel boundary per building would make multiple records overlap and double-count the same ground. The real building footprint is the only non-overlapping, honest shape for each one.
properties.notes: ~165,000 sq ft (Forell), five stories; the May 2000 Regents design-approval item for the building believed to be this one gives 170,965 gsf. Architect Pelli Clarke Pelli with Flad Architects; notable for early use in California of buckling-restrained braces designed and procured with Nippon Steel in Japan (Forell), not seismic base isolation. Opened 2004 per UCSF's history timeline ('Arthur and Toni Rembe Rock Hall opens at the Mission Bay campus', history.library.ucsf.edu/1990.html, which gives the year only). No cited source gives a different opening year. A Rock Hall design-award mention in April 2005 rests on a UCSF news page that could not be read (only its URL was seen), so it is not relied on here.
